## Overview

Add token embeddings and optional late chunking to `/v1/embeddings` and `LLM.embed`. This is the embedding entrypoint alternative to #61419, requested for comparison in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61419#issuecomment-6161948029. It uses the core from #60164 and RFC #58774.

## Claims

- With the `token_embed` task, both entrypoints return token vectors by default and chunk vectors when `late_chunking_params` is set.
- Chunk results include token and source ranges. The offline example uses `LLM.embed`; `LLM.encode` remains available.
- ORJSON responses reuse the existing ndarray encoder. Ordinary `embed` output and the `/pooling` schemas are unchanged.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| CPU protocol, metadata, routing and output suites | 87 passed |
| E5 token embedding HTTP suite | 18 passed with each runner |
| E5 token embedding offline checks | 10 passed with each runner |
| Existing ordinary embedding offline and HTTP checks | 8 and 3 passed |
| Updated offline example | Prints chunk vectors and source ranges for both documents |

GPU checks use an A100 80GB and `intfloat/multilingual-e5-small` at revision `614241f622f53c4eeff9890bdc4f31cfecc418b3`. The HTTP suite uses bfloat16 and a 512 token context. It checks ordinary token vectors against `/pooling`, chunk means against contextual token vectors, source offsets, concurrent requests and invalid inputs. These are correctness checks, not retrieval quality benchmarks.

GPU checks predate the final offline validation adjustment, which is covered by CPU tests. Model computation and HTTP handling are unchanged by that adjustment.

<details>
<summary>Test commands</summary>

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/test_late_chunking.py \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/test_factories.py \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/test_utils.py tests/test_outputs.py \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/embed/test_protocol.py \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_jina_ranking_io_processor_unit.py

for runner in 1 0; do
  VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=$runner .venv/bin/python -m pytest -v \
    tests/entrypoints/pooling/token_embed/test_online.py
  VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=$runner .venv/bin/python -m pytest -v \
    tests/entrypoints/pooling/token_embed/test_offline.py \
    -k 'test_str_prompts or test_token_ids_prompts or test_e5_late_chunking_mixed_requests or test_unsupported_tasks'
done
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -v \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/embed/test_offline.py
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -v \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/embed/test_online.py \
  -k 'test_basic or test_pooling_embed or test_use_activation'
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 .venv/bin/python \
  examples/pooling/token_embed/late_chunking_offline.py --chunk-size 16
```

</details>

## Details

The handler reuses `TokenEmbedIOProcessor` and the existing chunk implementation. Route registration selects the schema for the configured task. Missing or null chunk parameters select ordinary token embeddings; malformed chunk parameters remain errors.

For offline `token_embed`, `LLM.embed` returns the existing `PoolingRequestOutput`, preserving its tensor matrix and chunk metadata. The `embed` task keeps its `EmbeddingRequestOutput` conversion. Existing `LLM.encode` validation rejects unsupported tasks and retains its configuration guidance.

For ColBERT, `LLM.embed` now returns token vectors instead of raising. Explicitly requesting `pooling_task="embed"` remains unsupported, which the updated ColBERT test checks. This does not change which models support late chunking.

The HTTP matrix-valued `embedding` and optional `late_chunking` metadata are a vLLM extension. Only float encoding is supported. Chunking requires plain text; ordinary token embeddings also accept token IDs. Ordinary `embed` servers do not enable chunking and can ignore an unrecognized `late_chunking_params` field. Cohere `/v2/embed`, the batch API and `/invocations` are not extended with chunking. On `token_embed` servers, `/v2/embed` is not registered, changing its unsupported API response from 501 to 404 for models advertising both tasks.

+
+| Field | Meaning |
+| --- | --- |
+| `strategy` | `"fixed_tokens"` |
+| `chunk_size` | Requested number of model-input tokens per chunk |
+| `input_tokens` | Number of tokens in this document, including special tokens |
+| `chunks` | One entry per vector row, containing `token_range` and `char_range` |
+
+Ranges have the same semantics as the offline API. JSON represents them as two-element arrays; `char_range` is `null` for a special-token-only chunk. Character indices count Unicode code points, so clients using UTF-16 string indices must convert them before slicing.
+
+Use a string or a nonempty list of strings as `input`. A batch shares one chunk size, returns one item per document in input order, and counts input tokens once in `usage`. Values of `chunk_size` larger than the input token count produce one chunk.
+
+Omit `late_chunking_params` or set it to `null` to return ordinary token vectors through the same endpoint. Each item then contains a token-vector matrix in `embedding` and omits `late_chunking`. This mode also accepts token IDs. With late chunking enabled, input must be plain text and must not request truncation or padding, because source ranges refer to the complete submitted text. Only `encoding_format="float"` is supported; chat messages and `dimensions` are unsupported by this endpoint.
+
+The matrix-valued `embedding` and `late_chunking` fields are a vLLM extension, not the standard OpenAI embedding response. Use an HTTP client that handles this format. Ordinary `embed` servers keep their existing response format; they do not enable late chunking and may ignore an unrecognized `late_chunking_params` field. Cohere `/v2/embed`, the batch API, and `/invocations` are not extended with late chunking.

+
+The [retrieval example](../../../examples/pooling/token_embed/late_chunking_retrieval_online.py) uses the server above to:
+
+1. Encode documents with E5's `passage:` prefix and request contextual chunks.
+2. Build an in-memory index containing vectors, document IDs, chunk indices and source ranges.
+3. Encode a question with the `query:` prefix, using one chunk covering the whole query.
+4. Rank stored vectors by cosine similarity and print the matching source excerpts.

+    --chunk-size 16 --query "Which city has museums with art collections?"

+
+Add `--index-path late_chunking_index.json` to save the index. The example creates no index file by default.
+
+For E5, one chunk covering the complete query produces its mean-pooled sequence embedding. Other models may require a different query head. Keep the model revision, prefixes, projection and normalization consistent between indexing and querying.
+
+Source ranges refer to the exact submitted text, including the prefix. The example excludes special-token-only chunks from retrieval. Fixed token boundaries may split sentences; late chunking does not guarantee better retrieval on every dataset.
+

+
+Use the [Pooling API](README.md#pooling-api) with `"task": "token_embed"` to return token vectors. The Pooling API does not support late chunking.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+
+"""Index contextual chunks and retrieve source excerpts with multilingual E5.
+
+Start the server with:
+    vllm serve intfloat/multilingual-e5-small --runner pooling \
+        --pooler-config.task token_embed --max-model-len 512
+
+Then run this file to search an in-memory index. Use --index-path to save it.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import numpy as np
+import requests
+
+
+def encode(session, args, texts, chunk_size):
+    response = session.post(
+        f"{args.url.rstrip('/')}/v1/embeddings",
+        json={
+            "model": args.model,
+            "input": texts,
+            "encoding_format": "float",
+            "use_activation": True,
+            "late_chunking_params": {"chunk_size": chunk_size},
+        },
+        timeout=120,
+    )
+    response.raise_for_status()
+    return response.json()["data"]
+
+
+def main(args):
+    # Ranges refer to these exact submitted strings, including the E5 prefix.
+    documents = {
+        "berlin": "passage: Berlin is the capital of Germany. The city has many "
+        "museums. They display art and historical collections from around the world.",
+        "kyoto": "passage: Kyoto is a city in Japan. Its historic temples attract "
+        "visitors throughout the year.",
+        "storage": "passage: Database backups protect data from accidental loss. "
+        "They should be tested regularly to ensure that recovery works.",
+    }
+    chunks = []
+    with requests.Session() as session:
+        outputs = encode(session, args, list(documents.values()), args.chunk_size)
+        for doc_id, output in zip(documents, outputs):
+            for index, (vector, chunk) in enumerate(
+                zip(output["embedding"], output["late_chunking"]["chunks"])
+            ):
+                if chunk["char_range"] is None:
+                    continue  # No source text to retrieve for special-only chunks.
+                chunks.append(
+                    {
+                        "document_id": doc_id,
+                        "chunk_index": index,
+                        "vector": vector,
+                        **chunk,
+                    }
+                )
+
+        # E5 uses mean pooling. One chunk covering the query gives its sequence
+        # embedding, with the same model, head and normalization as the documents.
+        # The server rejects queries longer than its 512-token context window.
+        query = encode(session, args, [f"query: {args.query}"], chunk_size=512)[0]
+        (query_embedding,) = query["embedding"]
+        query_vector = np.asarray(query_embedding, dtype=np.float32)
+
+    if args.index_path is not None:
+        args.index_path.write_text(
+            json.dumps(
+                {
+                    "model": args.model,
+                    "chunk_size": args.chunk_size,
+                    "documents": documents,
+                    "chunks": chunks,
+                },
+                ensure_ascii=False,
+            ),
+            encoding="utf-8",
+        )
+        print(f"Saved {len(chunks)} chunks to {args.index_path}")
+    vectors = np.asarray([chunk["vector"] for chunk in chunks], dtype=np.float32)
+    scores = vectors @ query_vector  # Cosine similarity for normalized vectors.
+    for index in np.argsort(-scores)[: args.top_k]:
+        chunk = chunks[index]
+        start, end = chunk["char_range"]
+        excerpt = documents[chunk["document_id"]][start:end]
+        print(
+            f"{scores[index]:.4f} {chunk['document_id']} "
+            f"chunk {chunk['chunk_index']}: {excerpt!r}"
+        )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--url", default="http://localhost:8000")
+    parser.add_argument("--model", default="intfloat/multilingual-e5-small")
+    parser.add_argument("--chunk-size", type=int, default=16)
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--query", default="Which city has museums with art collections?"
+    )
+    parser.add_argument("--top-k", type=int, default=3)
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--index-path", type=Path, help="Optionally save the index as JSON."
+    )
+    main(parser.parse_args())

When `orjson` is available and callers choose a small chunk size (especially `1`) on a long-context, high-dimensional model, this eagerly expands the entire `[tokens, dimension]` tensor into nested Python lists and then validates every scalar through Pydantic. That bypasses the ndarray path used by `ServingEmbedding._openai_json_response` via `encode_pooling_output_float_or_ndarray` even though `json_response_cls` is `ORJSONResponse`; large token matrices can therefore create tens of millions of Python float objects, exhaust frontend memory, and block the shared preprocessing/postprocessing executor. Build the ORJSON payload with the ndarray fast path and retain `.tolist()` only for `JSONResponse`.

The classes are still separate in this update. I've moved the helper to `pooling/token_embed/`, added token embedding support to `LLM.embed`, and updated the offline example to use it.
